newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish central bank sees bright 1997 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Danish central bank sees bright 1997 outlook.

text.p: Denmark's central bank, the National Bank, said on Thursday that it saw economic prospects for 1997 as good, but warned against allowing wages and prices to rise too fast.
"The outlook for the Danish economy in 1997 is in many respects brighter than it has been for a long time," the bank said in its 1996 annual report.

"The prospect is for the economic upturn to gather momentum, wage and price rises are, from a historic perspective, moderate, the current account indicates a surplus and the public sector budget is expected to balance in 1997," it said.
But it added a warning on rising wages and the dwindling current account.

"There are for the time being some reservations that deserve special attention. Wage and price rises are higher than those of our trading partners weakening both our competitiveness and the balance of payments as well as employment," it said.

"The current account surplus is of a such a modest amount that it could quickly disappear. With a continued significant level of foreign debt it is essential that the current account surplus is preserved at least at its present level," it added.

Full-year 1996 data showed a current account surplus of 10.9 billion crowns, compared to 9.4 billion in 1995, but monthly figures show the balance going from a 0.2 billion surplus in October 1996 to a 6.6 billion deficit in November and a 2.3 billion shortfall in December. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
